title: reading-notes-llm-inference-ethan-walker
content:
Purpose: personal learning notes + quick experiment ideas after reading a few papers, blog posts, and ICLR/NeurIPS talks. Mostly sketchy; TODOs next steps at the end.

High-level takeaways (fast):
- Prefix/KV caching gives big perf wins for chat-like workloads where many requests share prefixes (est. 20-60% token cost reduction depending on cache hit rate).
- Quantization (4-bit, QLoRA-style or GPTQ) is now practical for inference but needs per-model calibration to avoid quality regressions on prompts we care about.
- Continuous batching + adaptive batching gives best throughput with bounded latency — but tricky to tune for tail-latency SLOs.
- Model distillation / smaller top-layer models for classification/rerank can reduce cost a lot when full generative capability is not required.

Papers / posts skimmed (notes):
1) "KV-Cache Optimizations for Low-Latency Streaming" (blog + code):
   - Key idea: store persistent KV cache for repeated contexts (e.g., system prompts, repeated instructions).
   - Implementation notes: need eviction policy by recency and by usefulness (maybe use token-level attention weight heuristics).
   - Pitfall: memory blowup for many concurrent users unless we shard/persist cache per-session with expiry.
   - My note: experiment with LRU + size cap per-session = 8KB, measure hit rate on real chat traces.

2) "GPTQ and 4-bit inference tradeoffs" (paper + bench):
   - Quantization reduces memory footprint significantly and enables larger batching on the same GPU.
   - Quality: on summarization tasks, small BLEU/ROUGE drop but sometimes higher hallucination rates depending on scale.
   - My note: add a per-prompt quality-check automated eval (small eval set) after quantization rollout; consider model-specific scale factor tuning.

3) "Adaptive Batching for Online LLM Serving" (sysml/NeurIPS talk):
   - Dynamic batching with latency targets: form batches when either batch size threshold or wait timeout hit, but choose timeout adaptively based on recent arrival rate and SLO slack.
   - Tradeoff: more aggressive batching improves throughput but increases median and tail latency. We should expose policy knobs (latency target, max_batch, min_wait).
   - My note: prototype adaptive policy in serving-runtime v2 and simulate with replayed production traces (use AIINF-123 ticket trace).

4) "Model Routing and Fallbacks" (Redwood internal blog + external references):
   - Route requests to cheaper model variants for low-risk prompts; fallback to larger models when quality metrics drop.
   - Need reliable signal for quality risk: prompt classifiers, prompt length heuristics, user tier, or explicit metadata.
   - My note: create a small classifier to detect "high-risk" prompts (legal/medical/long-context) and A/B test routing policy.

Concrete experiments to run (short-term):
- E1: KV cache hit-rate measurement (2 weeks)
  - Data: sample 1M chat requests from AIINF-123 (sanitized).
  - Metric: prefix hit rate, tokens saved, per-user memory cost.
  - Success: >25% token savings for active chat users w/o >10% memory bloat.

- E2: Quantization QA run (3 weeks)
  - Models: Llama-2-13b, OpenFLan-7b (where available).
  - Steps: run baseline eval (multitask QA + summarization), apply GPTQ 4-bit quant, run eval.
  - Metric: delta accuracy/ROUGE < 2% absolute for core tasks; latency and throughput improvement >1.8x.
  - Rollout plan: canary on dedicated pool, gated by eval and canary logs.

- E3: Adaptive batching sim + canary (4 weeks)
  - Simulate with replayed trace and estimate p50/p95/p99 latency vs throughput.
  - Canary: enable adaptive policy for 5% of traffic on dedicated cluster; monitor errors and latency.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How do we index/evict caches securely for Private deployments (customer isolation + KMS/HSM)? Need to align with private-deployments team.
- For quantized models, what is the best near-term tooling for per-model calibration? Do we build this in serving-runtime or rely on external toolchain?
- How to get robust online quality signals for model routing? User feedback is noisy; need automated eval hooks (prompt-level tests).

Links & refs (quick):
- KV cache notes (internal Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/987654321/KV+Cache+and+prefix+caching
- Ticket trace for experiment: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/AIINF-123
- Serving runtime PR with initial adaptive batching prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/456
- GPTQ implementation notes: https://github.com/ISTmodel/gptq (external), plus blog posts (distill).

TODOs (for me / quick next steps):
- [ ] Pull 1M sanitized chat sessions and compute prefix overlap histogram (owner: Ethan) — due 2025-11-21
- [ ] Spawn small quantization eval infra (use dev cluster, tag: quant-eval) and run baseline vs 4-bit (owner: Maya) — due 2025-11-28
- [ ] Sync with private-deployments on cache persistence/teardown (owner: Raja) — set meeting 2025-11-14
- [ ] Draft short proposal for A/B test of routing policy and quality signals (owner: Ethan) — draft by 2025-11-18

Notes to self / scribbles:
- Consider TTL vs absolute size caps per session; TTL may be simpler but less efficient for bursty users.
- Could use bloom filters for quick negative cache checks to avoid deserializing large cache blobs for unlikely hits.
- Track memory per-GPU if we shard caches in GPU DRAM vs host RAM; tradeoffs for latency.
- Remember to update ops-runbook if we enable persistent caches (eviction, crash recovery).

If useful, I can spin up a small lightweight doc with experiment templates (metrics + dashboards + alert thresholds) to hand to SRE/ops. Will do next after initial measurement.

End of notes.
